idea-plugin.name: Jeffrey Microscope
idea-plugin.description:
Jump from a JFR flame graph straight to your code.

Jeffrey Microscope is the companion IDE plugin for Jeffrey, a tool for analyzing Java Flight Recorder (JFR) recordings and heap dumps. While you explore a flame graph, a heap-dump view, or any other Microscope view, this plugin lets you click a stack frame or a class and land on the exact line of source in your already-open IntelliJ window.

The plugin stays out of your way — no toolbars, no tool windows, and a single context-menu action. It runs quietly in the background and enriches Jeffrey Microscope, letting Microscope discover your open IntelliJ projects and either navigate straight to the matching code or download the sources back into the application directly.

What it does

  • Frame-to-source navigation — resolves a fully-qualified class and method to a file, line, and column, opens it, and brings the IDE window to the front.
  • Inline source — serves source text back to Microscope so it can show code next to the profile, preferring attached sources over decompiled .class files.
  • Frame lookup without the jump — answers where a class and method live so an AI coding agent working through Microscope can ground its findings in real files and lines, without your editor moving while you work.
  • Send a recording for analysis — right-click a JFR recording, a heap dump, or a pprof/OpenTelemetry profile — compressed forms included — and open it straight in Microscope.
  • Recordings you can spot — every file that action accepts is drawn with the Jeffrey flame icon in the project tree and editor tabs, including the formats IntelliJ has no icon for at all.
  • A recording panel in the editor — open a recording and its tab tells you whether Microscope has analysed it, offers the button that does, and lays the views out as tiles: flame graph, allocations, GC, threads, traces and the rest, each with a line on what the page answers. A ready profile also shows its recording window, sample count, event types, sample loss and the auto-analysis findings. Views the recording has no data for stay visible but dimmed.
  • Checkout awareness — reports the branch and commit each window is on, so Microscope can warn when a profile describes different code than you have open.
  • Zero configuration — Microscope discovers the IDE automatically over IntelliJ's built-in server; there is nothing to pair or paste.

Private by design

  • Listens on localhost only — never reachable from the network.
  • Honors IntelliJ's trusted projects: untrusted projects are never navigated.
  • Toggle it off anytime under Settings → Tools → Jeffrey Plugin; a disabled IDE is completely invisible to Microscope.

Requires a running Jeffrey Microscope instance. Learn more at jeffrey-analyst.cafe.

action.description: Open this JFR recording or heap dump in Jeffrey Microscope
